newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends down with volume hit 96 high.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends down with volume hit 96 high.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended sharply down on Friday with volume hitting a 1996 high due to heavy overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active January 1997 contract ended at 20,500 yuan ($2,468) per tonne, losing 700 yuan. It opened limit-down at 20,460 and hit a high of 20,570.
September fell 200 to 21,200 yuan, October 450 to 20,800, November 610 to 20,520, December 760 to 20,480, February 700 to 20,500 and March 670 to 20,520.
Combined volume rose sharply to 121,750 tonnes from 39,090.
All later-maturing contracts opened limit-down and moved in a narrow range at low levels during most of the session.
Traders said losses on the LME triggered panic selling which would lead to further falls in the next few days.
"Panic stop-loss selling made most contracts open limit- down and the weak market sentiment will push them down further," one trader said.
"But heavy volume of trading at low levels indicated fresh buying and the desire of many investors to liquidated their short positions at this level," he added.

"Stop-loss orders are likely to push copper down on next Monday, but it will find strong support at the 20,000-yuan level because short position holders would have already made enough profits," a second trader said.
Analysts said copper would follow the LME's trend in the next few days due to a lack of domestic market-moving news.
Aluminium ended down. September fell 40 to 14,300 yuan, October 90 to 14,300 and November 80 to 14,320.
Combined volume rose to 610 tonnes from 240.
